Paragraph:
Translation: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus, Arjuna, chastiser of enemies, told Krsna, "Govinda, I shall not fight," and fell silent.

Purport: Dhrtarastra must have been very glad to understand that Arjuna was not going to fight and was instead leaving the battlefield for the begging profession. But Sanjaya disappointed him again in relating that Arjuna was competent to kill his enemies (parantapah)... This indicated that he would soon be free from the false lamentation resulting from family affection and would be enlightened...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna issues his final, definitive statement of refusal and completely shuts down.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Arjuna explicitly states, 'I shall not fight,' and goes completely silent. However, Sanjaya still refers to him as 'parantapah' (chastiser of enemies), hinting that this state is temporary and his true nature will resurface.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna enters a state of total withdrawal, waiting entirely on Krishna's response.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Tusnim babhuva (Becoming completely silent; the cessation of material argument before receiving divine knowledge)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Arjuna's silence signifies the end of his reliance on his own mind and ego. He has emptied his cup. By declaring his inability to act and falling silent, he creates the absolute void that Krishna's divine instructions will now fill.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This is a classic trauma response: freeze and shutdown. Having exhausted all his intellectual defenses and emotional outbursts, Arjuna’s nervous system simply powers down. He speaks his final boundary ('I shall not fight') and withdraws into silence, unable to process any further on his own.
